study_identification_part.si_4_title: Contrasting Case-Control and Normative Reference Approaches to Capture Clinically Relevant Structural Brain Abnormalities in Patients With First-Episode Psychosis Who Are Antipsychotic Naive

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used the Predictive Clinical Neuroscience and brain charts toolkits, which employ generalized additive models of location and shape (GAMLSS) to estimate normative models.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We quantified individual deviations for each region ... based on a normative reference model (n = 58 836) using the Predictive Clinical Neuroscience and brain charts toolkits (Figure 1). ... Normative modeling of neuroimaging data using generalized additive models of location and shape

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Subcortical volumes (thalamus, hippocampus, amygdala, ventral diencephalon, brainstem, caudate, putamen) and ventricle volumes were quantified.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: We quantified subcortical and ventricle volumes ... FEP had lower thalamus ... hippocampus ... amygdala ... ventral diencephalon ... and brainstem volumes.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative model used Age and Sex. Site effects were handled by transferring the model to the new site using healthy controls.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: We included age and sex, the same variables relevant in normative modeling ... To transfer the normative models to new sites, healthy controls from the new data set are used to learn site effects.
